comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
5377C350DFE80131041C68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

53776920DFE80131041B68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

53762460DFE80131041768A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

537586C0DFE80131041568A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

524CAE70DFE80131026B68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

524C60C0DFE80131026A68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

524AEB90DFE80131026668A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

524A2C00DFE80131026468A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

51AD9C70DFE8013101FB68A86D17958E.description: Explain various types of decision-making processes to enhance health or reduce health risks (e.g., automatic, intuitive, etc.). ATOD, IP/S, NUT

51AD5760DFE8013101FA68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish when individual or collaborative decision-making is appropriate. CEH, ATOD, VP/B

51AD15E0DFE8013101F968A86D17958E.description: Problem Solving and Decision Making: Students will use critical thinking and systematic processes to examine health related problems and make decisions that enhance health and reduce or avoid health risks.

51ACD260DFE8013101F868A86D17958E.description: Analyze characteristics of products and how they enhance health or reduce health risks (e.g., compare products). NUT, IP/S, PA

51AC8930DFE8013101F768A86D17958E.description: Analyze health information for characteristics of validity (e.g. compare and contrast currency of info in different health articles on ATOD, Violence or mental/emotional health). ATOD, ME, VP/B

51AC48B0DFE8013101F668A86D17958E.description: Explain criteria for determining validity of health information. SEXUALITY, ATOD, NUT

51AC04C0DFE8013101F568A86D17958E.description: Analyze situations or conditions to determine when health services are needed (e.g., Distinguish when symptoms warrant a visit to the doctor versus taking over the counter medication.). ME, VP/B, SEXUALITY

51ABC210DFE8013101F468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to locate appropriate health resources at school or in the community that help reduce health risks. SEXUALITY, ATOD, VP/B

51AB7B90DFE8013101F368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to locate appropriate health resources at school or in the community that help enhance health. ME, PH, NUT

51AB13D0DFE8013101F268A86D17958E.description: Health Information, Products and Resources: Students will access, analyze and evaluate health information, products and resources.

546CCAFB76B5454FA76118DA1A053C63.description: Students use a variety of methods including oral, written, graphic, pictorial, and/or multimedia in order to create and share a product.

F9764650FB774455870D008680ECE8A4.description: Technical Literacy: Students effectively read, evaluate, write, and communicate technical information.

D0EBB214E685472EB7DBC70E2DAB9A64.description: Students seek help from appropriate people (staff, students, parents, etc.) and appropriate resources.

C891E936194F41A68167B0275208155F.description: Students identify and practice compromise and conflict resolution skills.

D98BCEE147744CE4AC86E84666EB73C6.description: Communication and Collaboration: Students develop the skills necessary to effectively lead, collaborate, and communicate.

728A1DA46E2145C080DEF7842F779BFB.description: Students identify and demonstrate behaviors contributing to the successful completion of workplace tasks.

72C8308F2A3D435B9506A9FE7EC79558.description: Students describe how work relates to meeting needs for goods, clothing, shelter, and other necessities for living.

2A1FA2166A124B5383C4FE4C913E2950.description: Students identify and describe various occupations.

56898B20DFE80131079468A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.

5688F5A0DFE80131079268A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at school that are colorful).

56889830DFE80131079168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites (antonyms).

56884D10DFE80131079068A86D17958E.description: Sort common objects into categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

56880150DFE80131078F68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

5687B4B0DFE80131078E68A86D17958E.description: Use the most frequently occurring inflections and affixes (e.g., -ed, -s, re-, un-, pre-, -ful, -less) as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word.

56876610DFE80131078D68A86D17958E.description: Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately (e.g., knowing duck is a bird and learning the verb to duck).

56871120DFE80131078C68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on kindergarten reading and content.

56857740DFE80131078868A86D17958E.description: Spell simple words phonetically, drawing on knowledge of sound-letter relationships.

56853120DFE80131078768A86D17958E.description: Write a letter or letters for most consonant and short-vowel sounds (phonemes).

5684A630DFE80131078568A86D17958E.description: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I.

56845F10DFE80131078468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

56841730DFE80131078368A86D17958E.description: Produce and expand complete sentences in shared language activities.

5683C8C0DFE80131078268A86D17958E.description: Use the most frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with).

56837530DFE80131078168A86D17958E.description: Understand and use question words (interrogatives) (e.g., who, what, where, when, why, how).

56832EF0DFE80131078068A86D17958E.description: Form regular plural nouns orally by adding /s/ or /es/ (e.g., dog, dogs; wish, wishes).

5682E7C0DFE80131077F68A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring nouns and verbs.

56829FD0DFE80131077E68A86D17958E.description: Print many upper- and lowercase letters.

56825590DFE80131077D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

568148E0DFE80131077A68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

5680FBB0DFE80131077968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

5680B110DFE80131077868A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

567FFF70DFE80131077668A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

567F6890DFE80131077468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

567F0CA0DFE80131077368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

567E6420DFE80131077168A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

567E1D80DFE80131077068A86D17958E.description: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly.

567DD370DFE80131076F68A86D17958E.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions as desired to provide additional detail.

567D8BB0DFE80131076E68A86D17958E.description: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events and, with prompting and support, provide additional detail.

567CE840DFE80131076C68A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.

567C8820DFE80131076B68A86D17958E.description: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not understood.

567C31F0DFE80131076A68A86D17958E.description: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.

567BE650DFE80131076968A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).

567B9CE0DFE80131076868A86D17958E.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about kindergarten topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

567A9790DFE80131076568A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

567A4810DFE80131076468A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

5679FCD0DFE80131076368A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

56794F10DFE80131076168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

56790630DFE80131076068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

5678BC10DFE80131075F68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

56781A00DFE80131075D68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

567696B0DFE80131075968A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

56764920DFE80131075868A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of books by a favorite author and express opinions about them).

5675FA30DFE80131075768A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

56759E00DFE80131075668A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

56754F20DFE80131075568A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

56742FC0DFE80131075268A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or several loosely linked events, tell about the events in the order in which they occurred, and provide a reaction to what happened.

5673D560DFE80131075168A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory texts in which they name what they are writing about and supply some information about the topic.

56738C90DFE80131075068A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose opinion pieces in which they tell a reader the topic or the name of the book they are writing about and state an opinion or preference about the topic or book (e.g., My favorite book is…).

5672A760DFE80131074D68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

5671E980DFE80131074B68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

56719850DFE80131074A68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

56714C30DFE80131074968A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

56710010DFE80131074868A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

5670B300DFE80131074768A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

567062D0DFE80131074668A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

56700A30DFE80131074568A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

566F5400DFE80131074368A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

566EF270DFE80131074268A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

566E8A00DFE80131074168A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

566DFB00DFE80131073F68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

566DB370DFE80131073E68A86D17958E.description: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.

566D2270DFE80131073C68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.

566CD610DFE80131073B68A86D17958E.description: Read common high-frequency words by sight (e.g., the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does).

566C8250DFE80131073A68A86D17958E.description: Associate the long and short sounds with common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.

566C3740DFE80131073968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary or many of the most frequent sound for each consonant.

566BF080DFE80131073868A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

566B5CB0DFE80131073668A86D17958E.description: Add or substitute individual sounds (phonemes) in simple, one-syllable words to make new words.

566B0560DFE80131073568A86D17958E.description: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonent-vowel-consonent, or CVC) words. (This does not include CVCs ending with /l/, /r/, or /x/.)

566AA7B0DFE80131073468A86D17958E.description: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.

566A4C30DFE80131073368A86D17958E.description: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.

5669A9B0DFE80131073168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

5668D820DFE80131072F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.

56689170DFE80131072E68A86D17958E.description: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.

56684690DFE80131072D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.

5667F960DFE80131072C68A86D17958E.description: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.

5667AED0DFE80131072B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

5666C4F0DFE80131072868A86D17958E.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

5665DAE0DFE80131072568A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

56647CE0DFE80131072168A86D17958E.description: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.

56642ED0DFE80131072068A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

56636010DFE80131071E68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

566316C0DFE80131071D68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

5662CD30DFE80131071C68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

5661F170DFE80131071968A86D17958E.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

5660FEC0DFE80131071668A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.

56609A00DFE80131071568A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear (e.g., what moment in a story an illustration depicts).

565FD160DFE80131071368A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, name the author and illustrator of a story and define the role of each in telling the story.

565F88B0DFE80131071268A86D17958E.description: Recognize common types of texts (e.g., storybooks, poems).

565F4010DFE80131071168A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

565EA6D0DFE80131070F68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.

565E5570DFE80131070E68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, including key details.

565DE060DFE80131070D68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

565CFB80DFE80131070A68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

565C1780DFE80131070768A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

565BCAA0DFE80131070668A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

565954A0DFE8013106FE68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

4D95FFC3D88149529A75CD27FD82898C.description: Use digital tools to learn about social studies concepts.

F08DB3976B31403DB361D0795863AFB2.description: Identify what kinds of information can be found in different resources (e.g., library, computer, atlas, and dictionary).

3D8591A4ABBC474AA64E7A3399E9840F.description: Technology, Literacy, and Global Connections: Students use technology and literacy skills to access, synthesize, and evaluate information to communicate and apply social studies knowledge to global situations.

8C378DE35A79445DA8FD8EA81F780DC5.description: Identify how science or technology affects production (e.g., assembly line, robots, and video streaming).

88773679D48A439BA98851C046D3911F.description: Identify how price may affect buying, selling, and saving decisions.

900FDD79B0694DFBABEBFCC3E8F17D37.description: Give examples of and/or identify needs, wants, goods, and services.

AAFF70F3874B4F0099E523A111746734.description: Career-aware students demonstrate proficiency in selecting and utilizing technologies in the completion of tasks and projects.

12D75A53E9A54CAAAFF731BDF9294307.description: Career-aware students demonstrate technical knowledge and skills by safely, ethically and appropriately acquiring, storing, organizing and using materials, tools, and workspace.

0F0F10194E934AD69500908AE989FC10.description: Career-aware students plan tasks recognizing human resources, financial and timeline constraints that take into account priorities and goals.

2BCD48AA4DF74F279C8DE85EE2607713.description: Career-aware students identify technical and digital systems, how they are properly and ethically used and their relationship to other systems globally.

395DCB925C3D4130BF108A71850810F4.description: Technical Proficiency and Productivity: Students safely, ethically, and productively use existing and new technologies and systems.

A2BE6B07CC4D4FB8B7094BC38C2F4230.description: Career-aware students integrate and translate content presented in diverse formats and media, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

7431E45AE8D44343B4955346B1F4DE77.description: Career-aware students demonstrate the ability to create compositions and presentations of technical data in both written and verbal formats.

188BC8B23ADC4C25B073B0F20795E624.description: Career-aware students demonstrate an ability to identify sources from which they locate, interpret, extract and summarize data in an ethical and appropriate manner.

CE209AC8168F40A2971CD2FF9A1CDB31.description: Career-aware students produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization and style are appropriate to task, purpose and audience.

3964253B64F44BFD9A2CD4BE6394C909.description: Technical Literacy: Students effectively read, evaluate, write, and communicate technical information.

72DEF411A23746839FBBDD6E39DB6D42.description: Career-aware students plan, manage and complete projects in a timely and effective manner.

35F7E2F86CA042B7A63D036C77DD1ACD.description: Career-aware students demonstrate an ability to explain and interpret solutions to problems using data and information compiled from a variety of reputable sources.

A0B4C95FDBB14CB1B45110A17EDEBBE0.description: Career-aware students demonstrate an awareness of the working process of business and political systems and how they affect specific careers.

0B9312BBF42A4CA387C70784C14DD730.description: Career-aware students identify real-world problems and efficiently locate & effectively use various sources of information for informed decision making.

F209BD5BC0DF47EB8177F6B07F03CFF6.description: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: Students use critical thinking skills to plan and conduct research, manage projects, solve problems, and make informed decisions using appropriate technology, tools, and resources.

36568928FF334073AA8CBF101C681205.description: Career-aware students apply safe, legal, and responsible use of information and technology as appropriate to the task.

548BD8A791B1471E9AF1AF9A98DB5A4A.description: Career-aware students actively participate as a team member to accomplish group goals while effectively working with diverse individuals/groups.

45E0E4CD5C47418F988C5E93076F134C.description: Career-aware students successfully lead a group activity.

9B5651E8A14C498A80230F47BD700531.description: Career-aware students effectively communicate using a variety of appropriate methods.

AB92504CC85145D4B3E7D63F3A2B9E28.description: Communication and Collaboration: Students develop the skills necessary to effectively lead, collaborate, and communicate.

0F0C71CB869D4C8388082078BCB9DC18.description: Career-aware students demonstrate an awareness of characteristics and skills necessary to enhance employability.

5E50641AD9A841C9ACC8D8B2EA373E18.description: Career-aware students prepare a self-improvement plan including secondary and postsecondary programs to gain desired knowledge and experience toward possible career opportunities.

EC4F825ABF6A467FAB500CC4E9E27800.description: Career-aware students conduct an inventory of personal skills, aptitude and interests and identify career pathways that align with their results.

9F0EF2B5C60149C59EC9A97BB649FD3F.description: Career-aware students explore several career pathways including but not limited to outlook, salary, needed training, duties and lifestyle.

1F0B2D9250E249629D191DFA7986B703.description: Career Development and Readiness: Students demonstrate career planning and employability skills.

5629E8F0DFE8013106EA68A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate respect for individual differences and similarities in others in physical activity settings.

5629A1A0DFE8013106E968A86D17958E.description: Students demonstrate sportsmanship, cooperation, and teamwork in physical activity settings.

5628B000DFE8013106E568A86D17958E.description: Students recognize and explain valid characteristics of products and technology related to fitness literacy.

56281E60DFE8013106E368A86D17958E.description: Applying principles of fitness (FITT, warm-up/cool-down, progression, overload), students select and describe lifetime physical activities that enhance health related fitness.

5627DB70DFE8013106E268A86D17958E.description: Students explain and assess their personal fitness status in terms of cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition.

56279C00DFE8013106E168A86D17958E.description: Fitness: Students demonstrate fitness literacy and behaviors associated with it.

56271B00DFE8013106DF68A86D17958E.description:
Students explain critical skill elements or skill cues or key observation points associated with each of:
  1. rhythms or dance
  2. modified team activities
  3. regulation or individual or dual activities, and

5626D8E0DFE8013106DE68A86D17958E.description:
Students demonstrate skills in:
  1. rhythms or dance
  2. modified team activities
  3. regulation or individual or dual activities, and

57D366C0DFE801310A1768A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

57D304E0DFE801310A1668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

57D2B4D0DFE801310A1568A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

57D265D0DFE801310A1468A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

57D21BD0DFE801310A1368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

57D1D0E0DFE801310A1268A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

57D18050DFE801310A1168A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).

57D12840DFE801310A1068A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

57D0DF90DFE801310A0F68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

57D04C60DFE801310A0D68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

57CFA200DFE801310A0B68A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

57CF3190DFE801310A0A68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

57CE9540DFE801310A0868A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

57CE4D70DFE801310A0768A86D17958E.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

57CE0420DFE801310A0668A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

57CD5D70DFE801310A0468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

57CD0E90DFE801310A0368A86D17958E.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, two; there, their).

57CCC1A0DFE801310A0268A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

57CC2820DFE801310A0068A86D17958E.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

57CBCDE0DFE8013109FF68A86D17958E.description: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

57CB8340DFE8013109FE68A86D17958E.description: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

57CB3C60DFE8013109FD68A86D17958E.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

57CAF290DFE8013109FC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

57C9F840DFE8013109F968A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

57C99010DFE8013109F868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

57C92B00DFE8013109F768A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

57C89000DFE8013109F568A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

57C7E9C0DFE8013109F368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

57C78790DFE8013109F268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

57C6A060DFE8013109F068A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

57C65540DFE8013109EF68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

57C60860DFE8013109EE68A86D17958E.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

57C5BBE0DFE8013109ED68A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

57C51390DFE8013109EB68A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

57C4C690DFE8013109EA68A86D17958E.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

57C47F30DFE8013109E968A86D17958E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

57C43600DFE8013109E868A86D17958E.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

57C3EE40DFE8013109E768A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

57C3A320DFE8013109E668A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

57C34A20DFE8013109E568A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

57C24A40DFE8013109E268A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

57C1FC30DFE8013109E168A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

57C1A5F0DFE8013109E068A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

57C0D3F0DFE8013109DE68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

57C08CA0DFE8013109DD68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

57C04470DFE8013109DC68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

57BF9B60DFE8013109DA68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

57BF53F0DFE8013109D968A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

57BEC450DFE8013109D768A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text").

57BE78A0DFE8013109D668A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions].").

57BE22D0DFE8013109D568A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

57BDA490DFE8013109D468A86D17958E.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.

57BD36C0DFE8013109D368A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

57BCEDF0DFE8013109D268A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

57BCA4C0DFE8013109D168A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.

57BC56F0DFE8013109D068A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

57BBF9E0DFE8013109CF68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

57BB6030DFE8013109CD68A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

57BB17A0DFE8013109CC68A86D17958E.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

57BACDB0DFE8013109CB68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.

57BA82B0DFE8013109CA68A86D17958E.description: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

57BA2550DFE8013109C968A86D17958E.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situationand introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

57B9DD80DFE8013109C868A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

57B996E0DFE8013109C768A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented

57B94EC0DFE8013109C668A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

57B8FC40DFE8013109C568A86D17958E.description: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example, also, because).

57B8A490DFE8013109C468A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

57B83F80DFE8013109C368A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

57B7E730DFE8013109C268A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

57B79B50DFE8013109C168A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

57B74D70DFE8013109C068A86D17958E.description: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (e.g., for instance, in order to, in addition).

57B6FA50DFE8013109BF68A86D17958E.description: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.

57B6A080DFE8013109BE68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.

57B64D90DFE8013109BD68A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information

57B53590DFE8013109BA68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

57B48F70DFE8013109B868A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

57B444C0DFE8013109B768A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

57B3F520DFE8013109B668A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

57B39FE0DFE8013109B568A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

57B349C0DFE8013109B468A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

57B2E700DFE8013109B368A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

57B2A090DFE8013109B268A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

57B211E0DFE8013109B068A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

57B1C830DFE8013109AF68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

57B16CF0DFE8013109AE68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

57B0D140DFE8013109AC68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

57B074F0DFE8013109AB68A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

57B01350DFE8013109AA68A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

57AFC630DFE8013109A968A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

57AF6D20DFE8013109A868A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

57AEE0A0DFE8013109A668A86D17958E.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

57AE9840DFE8013109A568A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

57ADA6B0DFE8013109A268A86D17958E.description: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 4—5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

57AD5EC0DFE8013109A168A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

57AD16D0DFE8013109A068A86D17958E.description: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.

57ACCC60DFE80131099F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.

57AC7E10DFE80131099E68A86D17958E.description: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs, diagrams, time lines, animations, or interactive elements on Web pages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.

57ABC600DFE80131099C68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.

57AB70C0DFE80131099B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.

57AB20A0DFE80131099A68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.

57AA6B50DFE80131099868A86D17958E.description: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.

57AA1EA0DFE80131099768A86D17958E.description: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.

57A9D4C0DFE80131099668A86D17958E.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

57A8C710DFE80131099368A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4—5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

57A86020DFE80131099268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

57A7C780DFE80131099068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.

57A6CAB0DFE80131098D68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.

57A62160DFE80131098B68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (e.g., Herculean).

57A58DD0DFE80131098968A86D17958E.description: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions).

57A53470DFE80131098868A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.

57A4E750DFE80131098768A86D17958E.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

57A41250DFE80131098468A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

57A33140DFE80131098168A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

57A2E9F0DFE80131098068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

57A21770DFE80131097D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

57A1CB30DFE80131097C68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

535EFE30DFE80131041268A86D17958E.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.

535EB270DFE80131041168A86D17958E.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

535E56C0DFE80131041068A86D17958E.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

535DFB20DFE80131040F68A86D17958E.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

comments: For example, find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?
535DA470DFE80131040E68A86D17958E.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.

comments: For example, if a student is selected at random from a class, find the probability that Jane will be selected and the probability that a girl will be selected.
535D5A00DFE80131040D68A86D17958E.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

535D0E90DFE80131040C68A86D17958E.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

535CB5E0DFE80131040B68A86D17958E.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.
comments: For example, when rolling a number cube 600 times, predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly 200 times, but probably not exactly 200 times.

535C6620DFE80131040A68A86D17958E.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around 1/2 indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

535C2530DFE80131040968A86D17958E.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

535BE150DFE80131040868A86D17958E.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
comments: For example, decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth-grade science book.

535B50A0DFE80131040668A86D17958E.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

comments: For example, the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its width?

53583A90DFE8013103FC68A86D17958E.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.

534DF4D0DFE8013103D968A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

534DA870DFE8013103D868A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.
534C6860DFE8013103D468A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

comments: Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.
